discovered_problem: The frozen Evaluation Sample Registry exposed the acceptance split to Stage 12 evaluation in the top-level consumer contract but did not grant the evaluator at record level, leaving the declared Producer-to-Consumer boundary contradictory and making the Stage 11 audit hash stale after the boundary repair.

evidence.detail: Stage 12 requires an independent holdout entrypoint and the Registry is the single split-consumer authority.
The Stage 12 evaluator could not be reconciled with the acceptance record allowlist without a Registry change.
Stage 11 exit input hash changed when the Registry consumer boundary was corrected and required downstream rebuild.

why_change_is_required: This is a consumer-permission consistency defect; it is required to make the independent holdout evaluator explicit without granting development or reserve access.
alternatives_considered: Grant the evaluator access to all Registry splits
Grant only acceptance_holdout records and declare forbidden splits
reason_alternatives_rejected: Ignoring the contradiction leaves the Registry non-authoritative
The narrow allowlist matches the Stage 12 holdout contract
